hints.title: Convert the fourth root
hints.body: For x>0, the fourth root of x3 is x34. Expand the numerator (x2+5)(2x) before splitting the fraction.
hints.recap: Roots and quotients can be rewritten as sums of powers.
hints.pause: Write the two numerator terms divided by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Roots and quotients can be rewritten as sums of powers.

hints.title: Subtract denominator exponents
hints.body: Simplification gives f(x)=2x94+10x14. Apply the power rule separately to both terms.
hints.recap: In a quotient of powers, subtract exponents; in differentiation, subtract one.
hints.pitfall: Do not perform the integration rule by adding one.
hints.pause: Find the new coefficients and exponents.

recall.reminder: In a quotient of powers, subtract exponents; in differentiation, subtract one.

hints.title: Check the small exponent
hints.body: Differentiating x14 creates x−34. Check this sign as well as the coefficient 10×14.
hints.recap: Fractional powers may become negative powers after differentiation.
hints.pitfall: A negative exponent does not make the coefficient negative.
hints.pause: Compare both terms, not only the first, with the options.

recall.reminder: Fractional powers may become negative powers after differentiation.

solution:
The denominator is x34, and the numerator expands to 2x3+10x. Thus f(x)=2x3−34+10x1−34=2x94+10x14.

Using the power rule gives f′(x)=2(94)x54+10(14)x−34=(92)x54+(52)x−34, option B. All manipulations are valid on the stated domain x>0.
knowledgePattern: Simplify a radical quotient into powers before differentiating
